insights.title: Positive-integer expansions,selection and coefficient constraints
insights.teaching_comparison: YM develops repeated-product/Pascal investigations before full expansions,ordered leading terms,general-term selection,Laurent powers and product/parameter constraints. It separates factorial notation from the theorem. Its Example51adds two expansions;39and47multiply them. The retained Goldie2&3source assumes this Mathematics1background and supplies only small algebraic facets such as polynomial multiplication;its excluded generalised-binomial material is not a substitute for8227positive-integer scope. The census records that asymmetry rather than inventing a parallel Goldie progression.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2021P1Q1and2023P1Q4pair leading expansion with a product coefficient condition;2022P1Q3and2025P1Q2combine sums/differences;2024P1Q3selects a Laurent constant term. YM closely practises each direction but also recovers unknownn,discusses Pascal patterns and uses reciprocal multipliers. A textbook investigation rationale is not an official award criterion. ERR02 supports preserving an explicit HENCE dependency generally,not a claim that every coefficient question has one.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: GradeE02,C02andA02all retain positive-integern,and exclude required knowledge of greatest term/properties of coefficients. The difficulty difference lies in ordering,total-degree collection,allcontributing pairs and parameter filtering. Investigation of row patterns is labelled textbook-derived support,not newly required syllabus scope. QUAL03is checked on actual outer powers,not fractional inner coefficients.
insights.pitfalls: YM37has truncated/sign-wrong keys;Try46Q1has a wrong-variable independent-term prompt;Try47Q1needs an originally higher term because its multiplier is reciprocal. These recorded source defects matter more than agreement with a short key. The textbook warns through worked sequencing against omitted scale/sign factors;no specific examiner-frequency claim for each is made here.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM offers a much broader positive-integer progression than the retained Goldiebook. A position in original factor order can differ from descending-variable order;constant term and coefficient are not the same output. Book patterns beyond the prescribed knowledge remain supporting evidence. No textbook family count estimates future exam variety.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose explicit requested-order and target-exponent metadata,independent polynomial/convolution checks and complete parameter branch filtering. Preserve leading-expansion→coefficient chains. Keep empty impossible-index cases only where pedagogically warranted;avoid generalised-binomial generators or greatest-term requirements in8227.

insights.title: Recognition,term/sum constraints and contextual progression models
insights.teaching_comparison: YM first classifies lists,then makes unknown terms AP/GP,before direct terms,index membership,finite sums,inverse counts and mixed contexts. It contrasts NEXTblocks with initial blocks and decreasing with increasing sequences. Goldie2&3assumes these Mathematics1skills;the retained corpus has no comparable standalone AP/GPexercise progression. Incidental geometric series in an unrelated derivation would be component support,not equivalent direct practice.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2022P1Q5(a)recovers APconstants from a term and a sum;2024P1Q4models pump extraction and first threshold;2021P1Q8compares yearly GP/APdonation totals;2025P1Q5connects GPtotals to APterms. YM additionally uses endpoint membership,possibly two valid term counts,shared indexed conditions,staircase diagrams,investment timing and stock depletion. These broaden practice without supplying official awards or examination frequency.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E02names AP/GPrecognition and terms/sums;C02andA02retain progression problem solving. Harder tasks require integer selection,negative-ratio parity,correlated branches,calendar/block indexing or a model inferred from geometry. A large count alone is not harder reasoning. Do not infer that every word problem is gradeaor every direct term is gradee.
insights.pitfalls: YMTry8Q9omits a valid zero APbranch;Try13Q7omits a negative GPratio;Example32has incompatiblecm/mdata. Example35payment timing is ambiguous,andExample33requires inclusive years. These are recorded source limitations. Textbook-advised adjacent-index verification is useful,but this synthesis claims no examiner-error frequency for these particular defects.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM provides routine drills and contexts beyond the sampled exam structures;the retained Goldiebookoffers no equivalent standalone sequence. Direct term thresholds and cumulative sum thresholds need different data contracts. AP/GPclassification can overlap in constant cases,and zero cases need an explicit ratio convention. A supplied staircase figure tests reading the first exceptional riser,not merely substituting into an APformula.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose a first-term/index ledger and adjacent-value checks for threshold branches;retain all positive integer counts unless least/greatest is actually asked. For contexts,make payment timing,calendar inclusion,stock versus flow and units explicit. Keep geometry-to-model and linked AP/GPbranches distinct from bare-formula drills.

insights.title: Sigma bounds and convergent infinite progressions
insights.teaching_comparison: YM explicitly asks expansion of Sigma notation before evaluation,reverses listed series into Sigma form,and then varies lower bounds,unknown upper bounds and infinite exponent shifts. It compares finite totals with the infinite limit before inverse-parameter and contextual recurring-decimal/rebound tasks. The retained Goldiebookdoes not provide a parallel direct sequence;its numerical-limit exposition should not be relabelled as AP/GPcoverage.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2022P1Q5(b)uses an infinite Sigmasum with a shifted lower bound;2023P1Q5separates show-geometric,convergence interval and inverse total;2024P1Q4(c)uses an infinite contextual total. YM adds notation-writing,remaining tails,squared-term sums,recurring decimal blocks and rebound segment ledgers. A formal convergence statement is only directly assessed when requested;it remains a validity condition for every infinite total.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E02includes Sigma;C02explicitly includes convergence and infinite sums. The hardest source branches involve parameter filtering,index shifts and two linked series rather than larger numerical terms. The boundary |r|=1must remain outside ordinary infinite GPsum use. No derivative convergence test or numerical fixed-point theorem is imported into this topic.
insights.pitfalls: YMExample30’s coefficient24is not its first term because the first exponent is1;Try31Q5requires filtering recovered values through convergence. Try28inequalities ask allinteger outcomes,not an unasked least one. Book recurring-decimal dot groupings need the render;the first rebound drop is unpaired. These are source/author cautions with no examiner-specific error-rate assertion.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM supplies strong indexing and convergence variety;Goldie’s retained content supplies no equivalent direct practice. Finite Sigma and infinite Sigma are separate validity cases;computing a total does not by itself demonstrate interpreting notation or justifying convergence. The original response requirements must remain visible.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose recording literal bounds and deriving first term/ratio from them,validating inverse solutions against |r|<1,and preserving notation→terms→sum when asked. Rebound assets should show the actual segment sequence. Recurring decimals need exact block notation and should stay labelled textbook-derived context.
